name: Coolie
lede: Coolie is a moderate purplish blue from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, filed here as historical data under a name now recognized as an ethnic slur.

sections.title: A dated, offensive name
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* dates this purplish blue to 1924, on plate 45, cell D12 [1]. In that period, "coolie" was a common but demeaning English word for indentured and low-wage Asian laborers; today it is widely recognized as an ethnic slur, and we record it here only as the historical dictionary entry, not as a name we recommend using [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 report classes the hue as a moderate purplish blue [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[liberty-blue]], [[corsican-blue]], [[imperial-blue]] and [[azurite-blue]], at 2.7, 3, 3.3 and 3.8 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this blue in 50 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.2 percent, as photographed [4]. It peaks sharply in the 1910s decade, with Vilhelm Lundstrøm, Bronzino and Henri Matisse among the painters who carry it most [4]. The count is a computed color match on photographed, varnished canvases, not a pigment identification [4].
